messages:
jamie-support: FYI incoming from AcmePayments — they started seeing spikes of 504s and long tail timeouts ~12:42 UTC. p95 jumped ~120ms -> 2.3s. Sample req: req_id=acme-req-9f3a. They repro with POST /v1/generate model=redwood-3b hosted payload ~1500 tokens. Attached snip of gateway log: ```504 gateway timeout; upstream_status=504; request_queue_depth=4096; batcher_queue_len=4200```
sara-eng: Which region/tenant and any recent deploys? Are errors spread across models or specific to 3b?
jamie-support: Hosted us-east-1, tenant=acme-payments, no deploys around that time. Customer reports success on immediate retry sometimes. Also saw some 429s earlier in the window.
opsbot: ALERT: metric request_queue_depth.acme-payments > threshold (4096) at 2026-03-17T12:43:10Z :raised_hands:
mike-oncall: grabbing traces now. Could be continuous-batcher backlog + queue depth cap. Can someone pull continuous_batcher.backlog, kv_cache.miss, and per-tenant queue depth?
sara-eng: metrics snapshot (12:44 UTC): continuous_batcher.backlog=~4200, request_queue_depth.limit=4096, kv_cache.miss_rate=0.47, batcher.max_batch_size=64, avg_seq_len=1200. Looks like tenant filled queue and is triggering hard-cap rejects/timeouts.
dana-cust-success: Customer is asking for an ETA — they have production traffic impacted. They need short mitigation.
mike-oncall: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) enable overflow pool for tenant so excess requests spill to extra workers; 2) temporarily raise tenant queue depth to 8192; 3) reduce max_batch_size to lower head-of-line blocking for long sequences. Prefer 1+3 to avoid blowout on overall scheduling. Which option do we want ops to run?
sara-eng: Agreed. Start with enabling overflow pool and throttle batch sizes. Prepare commands and notify customer.
jamie-support: quoting customer: "They see the request hang at gateway with 3xx/5xx after ~30s, then retry sometimes succeeds — they are retrying in prod which amplifies the queue."
---
Commands proposed:
```
# enable overflow for tenant
rictl tenant update acme-payments --overflow-pool enabled --region us-east-1
# reduce continuous batcher size for tenant
rictl serving set-config continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=32 --tenant acme-payments --region us-east-1
# (if needed) increase queue depth
rictl tenant update acme-payments --queue-depth 8192 --region us-east-1
# flush tenant kv cache
rictl kvcache flush --tenant acme-payments --region us-east-1
```
---
opsbot: running: rictl tenant update acme-payments --overflow-pool enabled --region us-east-1 (action requested by sara-eng)
opsbot: running: rictl serving set-config continuous_batcher.max_batch_size=32 --tenant acme-payments --region us-east-1
opsbot: running: rictl kvcache flush --tenant acme-payments --region us-east-1
infra-bot: scaled overflow pool +2 nodes in us-east-1 for tenant acme-payments (provisioning completed)
mike-oncall: Observed backlog drop: continuous_batcher.backlog 4200 -> 80 within ~90s after overflow + batcher change. kv_cache.miss fell to 0.12 after flush. Gateway 504s reduced.
jamie-support: Customer confirms errors dropped to near 0 and p95 returned to ~130ms. They will run a controlled load test and report. :thumbsup:
sara-eng: Root-cause notes: tenant traffic had a high proportion of very long sequences (~1200 tokens) which increases batch formation time; continuous_batcher watermarks didn't scale fast enough and queue cap hit hard. Follow-ups: 1) tune continuous_batcher autoscale thresholds for long-seq patterns; 2) add earlier overflow spill trigger (at 70% of queue_depth); 3) add per-tenant early-reject advisory to customers. Ticket created: INC-2026-312 (triage + follow-up).
dana-cust-success: I'll send the customer a summary and the next steps.
mike-oncall: Marking P1 mitigated. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours then close if stable.
